To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prepositional phrase is a grammaticalized linguistic device to conceptualise complex events; 2) the preposional phrase is a grammatically and cognitively closed lexical class; 3) prepositions provide a frame for abstract events; 4) the spatial meaning of prepositions is extended metaphorically; 5) this spatial meaning is experientially correlated with abstract phenomena.

(1) prepositions shape frames for complex abstract events; (2) the spatial-to-abstract extension of prepositions can be quantitatively modelled; and (3) the extension is systematic and can be predicted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How do spatial prepositions contribute to the construction of complex abstract events in the English language?
the cognitive mechanisms of conceptual metaphor and experiential correlation in the context of spatial prepositions in scientific texts.
the question of how prepositions shape frames for events and how these frames are used in academic writing in English.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prepositions in English science writing are not only used to describe spatial relations, but also serve the function of providing a cognitive frame to describe abstract events.
the use of prepositional phrases is an essential tool in the construction of scientific texts.
prepositions in science writing are used to create conceptualisations of abstract events and phenomena by mapping spatial relationships onto the abstract domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prepositions in academic texts from the natural sciences are not just spatial markers but are used to conceptualise and structure complex abstract events.
prepositions shape abstract frames for events in the natural sciences.

prepositions are not only a grammatical means for spatial reference, but that they also provide a conceptual frame that can be used in abstract contexts, where the referents cannot be perceived directly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prepositions are more than simple markers of spatiality, they are the building blocks for abstract conceptualisations in science.
the use of prepositional frames in academic discourse can be used to map spatial relationships to abstract events and phenomena in a systematic and predictable way.
prepositions are not only spatially motivated but also provide a cognitive access to complex events and phenomena in abstract domains.
